rationale: One major patch finding: handleRefresh has no catch block, so indexSettings failures are silently swallowed — the user gets no feedback when the refresh fails. All 11 acceptance criteria pass or are covered by the integration test suite. Concurrency and unmount edge cases raised by edge-case lens are real but pre-existing store-level concerns, deferred out of this PR's scope.

business_review.criterion: State WITH integrations: enabled dropdown visible
State WITH integrations: Refresh button to the right of dropdown
State WITH integrations: helper text 'Choose an existing integration, or add a new one and refresh the list.'
State WITHOUT integrations: disabled dropdown visible (not interactive)
State WITHOUT integrations: Refresh button visible
State WITHOUT integrations: helper text 'Create a user integration, or refresh the list after one is added.'
Refresh calls resetIsSettingsIndexed() THEN indexSettings() as required pair
After refresh, component reflects new data (dropdown repopulates)
business_review.notes: Covered end-to-end by integration test 'repopulates the dropdown after clicking Refresh when an integration becomes available'

business_review.criterion: Refresh button disabled while refresh is in progress
No 'Add User Integration' in panel footer when disabled

standards_review.notes: Branch follows EPMCDME-<ticket>_<slug> format consistent with recent project commits
TypeScript, Tailwind, React patterns consistent with codebase conventions
No security issues: no user input execution, no XSS vectors, no secret exposure

findings.problem: handleRefresh uses try/finally but has no catch block. If userSettingsStore.indexSettings() rejects (network error, API 500, auth failure), the error is silently swallowed — isRefreshing resets to false so the button re-enables, but the user receives zero feedback.
findings.impact: User clicks Refresh, the operation fails silently, the UI appears unchanged, and the user may incorrectly believe the refresh succeeded or that no integrations exist when the real cause is a transient server error.
findings.recommendation: Add a catch block that calls toaster.error() (the project-standard notification mechanism already used in this file's test mock): catch (e) { toaster.error('Failed to refresh integrations. Please try again.') }
